transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, it's very nice to meet you too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I guess I'm here because things have been just a little stressful at home, and I wanted to talk to someone to make sure I'm looking at things the right way. I hope that's an okay reason to come in? 

It’s mainly about my wife. For the past year or so, she’s been having these late meetings, and... well, I’ve noticed some little changes in her work messages. I know she says it’s all just normal office stuff, and I really don't want to sound unreasonable or suspicious—I know how this might come across—but... they’ve just lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It almost feels like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like they're meant to tell me something she just won’t say directly to me. 

Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm making sense.
Do you believe for certain that your wife is sending you hidden messages through her work communications?

Well... I mean, "for certain" is a strong way to put it, right? I wouldn't want to sound like I'm accusing her of anything bad. I really love her, and she's a wonderful person. 

But... yes, I suppose I do believe it. I know she says it's just normal office stuff, and maybe I'm overthinking it—I really hope I am—but for the past year, the late meetings and the little changes in how she writes her messages... they just line up too precisely. It doesn't feel accidental. It really does feel like there's a private signal in them, meant to tell me something she just won't say directly. 

Does that make sense? I know it sounds a little strange when I say it out loud... I just want to make sure you don't think I'm being a bad husband for noticing these things.
Do you think anyone besides your wife is involved in sending you these hidden messages?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I really hope I didn't make it sound like some kind of... big conspiracy or anything like that. That would be completely unreasonable, wouldn't it? 

It's really just... just my wife. I haven't noticed anyone else doing anything strange at all. Her coworkers and everyone else seem perfectly normal. I just... I don't want you to think I'm, you know, suspicious of everyone around me or looking for things that aren't there. It's just this one very specific thing with her messages that caught my eye. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I'm trying to be as clear as I can for you.
If your wife showed you clear proof that these messages were ordinary work communications, would you be able to accept that?

Well... I mean, I would certainly want to. I really would. If she sat down and showed me proof, I'd want to just say, "Okay, honey, I believe you," and put it all behind us. That's what a good husband should do, right? 

But... um... I think it would be really hard for me to just... accept it completely. Even if she showed me what looked like ordinary work emails, I just keep coming back to how the late meetings and those little changes in her messages have lined up for the past year. It’s just... it’s too precise. It really doesn't feel accidental. Even if the words look normal on the surface, it still feels like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like she's trying to tell me something she just won’t say directly. 

I know that probably sounds stubborn, and I really don't want to be a difficult person. I just... I can't seem to shake that feeling. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying that.
Have you heard or seen things that other people could not?

Oh, no, no. Nothing like that. I've never... um, I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. I know that's something people worry about sometimes, but my mind is perfectly clear in that way. 

I really just see and hear what everyone else does. It's just... the meaning behind the messages that I notice. But my eyes and ears are working just fine, I promise. I wouldn't want you to think I was losing touch with reality or anything like that. I'm a very grounded person, really. Does that help clear things up?
Before this started with your wife, did you generally tend to mistrust other people or suspect they had hidden motives?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I've always been a very trusting person, honestly. I've never been the type to look over my shoulder or think people are out to get me. I've always tried to see the best in everyone, you know? 

At work, at the university, I get along with all the students and the professors. I've always felt very comfortable around people and assumed they mean well. That's why this whole thing with my wife has been so... confusing for me. It's really out of character for me to feel this way. I just want to be sure you know that I'm not usually a suspicious or difficult person. I hope I'm making sense? I just don't want you to think I'm some kind of paranoid person who goes around doubting everyone.
Have you noticed your thoughts becoming confused or hard to organize?

No, not at all. My thoughts are... they're very organized, very clear. I mean, as a teaching assistant, I have to keep track of a lot of information, grade papers, organize lesson plans... and I haven't had any trouble with any of that. 

I'm actually very proud of how well I keep everything straight. Even with all this stress about my wife, I haven't let it affect my work or my ability to think clearly. I'm still very sharp, I promise. I wouldn't want you to think my mind was getting jumbled or anything. I'm answering your questions clearly, aren't I? I hope I'm being helpful.
During this past year, have you had a period when you felt unusually depressed for most of the day nearly every day?

Oh, depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, it's been a very stressful year with everything going on with my wife, and sometimes that makes me a little sad, but... not depressed. Not like what you're describing, where it's all day, every day. 

I still get up, I go to work, I interact with the students. I try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I wouldn't want to bring anyone else down. I've always been pretty good at just pushing through and staying cheerful, even when things are tough. I'm doing okay in that regard, really. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I've been doing.
Did this start soon after a major stress or conflict in your marriage?

Oh, no, definitely not. We didn't have any big blowups or... or anything like that. I mean, every marriage has its little everyday bumps, right? But nothing major at all. We've actually always had a very peaceful home life. 

I always try my best to be a good, supportive husband, you know, so we rarely argue. That's part of why this has all been so surprising to me. Everything was just completely normal and fine between us before I started noticing things. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to give you the most accurate picture I can, so please let me know if I'm explaining it okay.
Since this began, has your ability to work and manage your usual daily life gotten noticeably worse?

Oh, no, my daily life is still... it's still going really well, actually. I wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything. I still show up for all my teaching sections, I keep up with all the data analysis for the professor I work for... I even still make sure to ride my bike to stay healthy, and I meet my friends for chess on the weekends. 

I really try to keep everything on track. The only place it really... well, the main place it causes any trouble is just when my wife and I get stuck arguing about what her work schedule really means. But other than that, I'm managing everything else just fine. I'm keeping up with all my responsibilities, I promise. Does that sound like I'm handling things okay to you? I really want to make sure I'm giving you a good picture of how I'm functioning.
For how long have you been convinced that your wife is sending you hidden messages?

Well, convinced is... that sounds a bit strong, doesn't it? I don't want to make it sound like I'm obsessing over it or anything negative like that. I've just been noticing these little hints she leaves for me to figure out. 

As for how long, it's been going on for about a year now. It started right around the time she began working outside the home again. I always try to be a very attentive husband, you know, so I just naturally started picking up on the little things she was trying to communicate to me once she took that job. But yes, it's been about a year. I hope that gives you the specific timeframe you were looking for? I really just want to make sure I'm answering your questions exactly the way you need me to.
Do you believe the messages from your wife contain special powers or impossible meanings that ordinary communication could not have?

Oh, goodness, no. No special powers or anything impossible like that. I really wouldn't want you to think I believe in magic or... or anything out of touch with reality. I know how that would sound, and I promise I'm looking at this very logically. 

It's actually very ordinary. I know my wife says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. And I really do try to be understanding about her job and give her the benefit of the doubt. But... well, for the past year, they’ve just lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It's not supernatural, it's more like... like there’s a private signal in them, meant to tell me something she just won’t say directly to my face. 

It's just regular communication, just hidden beneath the surface. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it in a way that's helpful for you, I really don't want to make it sound stranger than it actually is.
Over this past year, have you noticed yourself feeling much less interested in socializing or in activities you usually enjoy?

No, not at all. I'm... I'm still very much involved with my friends and my hobbies. I wouldn't want you to think I'm isolating myself or getting depressed, because I'm really not. 

Like I mentioned before, I still meet my friends for chess on the weekends. We always have a good time. And I still really enjoy my bike rides. I think it's so important to stay active and keep up with the things you love, don't you? I make a real effort to stay connected and positive. I hope that shows you that I'm still functioning well and keeping a good balance in my life. Is that the kind of information you were hoping for?
Over the past year, have other people noticed that you seem emotionally flat or show much less facial expression or feeling than usual?

No, no one has said anything like that to me. I... I really try to be warm and present when I'm around people. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was ignoring them or, you know, just staring blankly. That would be so rude, and I pride myself on being polite. 

I'm pretty sure I still smile and react just like I always have. My friends at the chess club haven't mentioned anything, and I think they would if I was acting cold or... or flat, as you said. I really do make an effort to be engaging. I hope that reassures you? I'm trying very hard to be a good conversationalist, both with my friends and with you here today.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Over this past year, have you noticed yourself feeling much less interested in socializing or in activities you usually enjoy?

patient.answer:
No, not at all. I'm... I'm still very much involved with my friends and my hobbies. I wouldn't want you to think I'm isolating myself or getting depressed, because I'm really not.

doctor.question: Over the past year, have other people noticed that you seem emotionally flat or show much less facial expression or feeling than usual?

patient.answer:
No, no one has said anything like that to me. I... I really try to be warm and present when I'm around people. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was ignoring them or, you know, just staring blankly. That would be so rude, and I pride myself on being polite. 

I'm pretty sure I still smile and react just like I always have. My friends at the chess club haven't mentioned anything, and I think they would if I was acting cold or... or flat, as you said. I really do make an effort to be engaging. I hope that reassures you? I'm trying very hard to be a good conversationalist, both with my friends and with you here today.

inference.note: Persistent non-bizarre delusion for ~1 year with preserved functioning, no hallucinations, no thought disorder, and no negative symptoms rules against F20.0 and supports F22.
